data.label: Capture New Lead
data.description: Trigger when a new lead is submitted through the website form.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on form submission. No uncertainty, learning, or language understanding is required, so L0 is the correct level.
conditions: Incoming request matches lead submission schema
data.errorHandling: Return 4xx for malformed payloads; log request metadata; do not enqueue downstream steps if required fields are missing; retry only transient transport failures at the ingress layer.

data.label: Validate Email Format
data.description: Check that the submitted email address is syntactically valid.
data.rationale: Email syntax validation is pure rule-based logic using regex or equivalent deterministic checks. L0 fully covers this step; no ML or LLM is needed.
data.errorHandling: If the email is invalid, stop processing and route to an invalid-lead/error queue or end state with reason code; no retries are needed because the failure is data-related, not transient.

data.label: Check CRM Duplicates
data.description: Search the CRM for an existing contact or lead matching the new submission.
data.rationale: Duplicate checking can be done with deterministic database queries and exact or configured matching rules. This is standard L0 lookup/validation logic, not ML.
data.errorHandling: On CRM/API timeout, retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times; if still unavailable, send to a temporary review/retry queue; if a matching record exists, stop downstream processing and mark as duplicate.

data.label: Score Lead
data.description: Calculate a lead score using company size, industry, and engagement history.
data.rationale: Lead scoring is typically a predictive ranking/classification task where a model or learned weights estimate lead quality from structured features. L0 could implement a fixed rubric, but the presence of multiple features and scoring implies uncertainty and variation that is better handled by supervised ML at L1.
conditions: company size, industry, and engagement history are present or defaultable
data.errorHandling: If model inference fails, fall back to a deterministic rule-based score using available fields; if features are missing, impute defaults or flag for manual review; version and log model inputs for auditability.

data.label: Evaluate High Score
data.description: Determine whether the lead score is above 80 for sales routing.
data.rationale: This is a simple threshold comparison on a numeric score. It is deterministic branching and fits squarely in L0.
data.errorHandling: If score is missing or malformed, route to manual review and emit a data-quality alert; no retry is needed unless upstream scoring is transiently unavailable.

data.label: Evaluate Low Score
data.description: Determine whether the lead score is below 40 for nurture routing.
data.rationale: This is also a deterministic threshold check on the same numeric score. No learning or language interpretation is required, so L0 applies.
data.errorHandling: If score cannot be evaluated, route to manual review as a safe fallback and record the anomaly for investigation.

data.label: Build Personalized Summary
data.description: Create a personalized summary for the assigned sales rep using lead details and scoring context.
data.rationale: This step requires generating natural-language output tailored to the lead and the sales rep. That is a self-contained LLM generation task, which fits L3. No external tools are necessary based on the description.
conditions: lead profile and routing context available
data.errorHandling: If generation fails, fall back to a templated summary assembled from structured lead fields; cache the prompt and response metadata; retry once on transient model/API errors.

data.label: Route to Sales Rep
data.description: Assign the high-scoring lead to a sales representative.
data.rationale: Assigning a lead to a rep is a deterministic routing action, typically based on assignment rules, availability, or round-robin logic. This is L0 automation.
conditions: summary generated or fallback summary available
data.errorHandling: If assignment fails, retry the CRM update up to 3 times for transient errors; on persistent failure, place the lead in an unassigned queue and notify operations.

data.label: Add to Nurture Campaign
data.description: Enroll low-scoring leads into the nurture campaign.
data.rationale: Adding a lead to a campaign is a straightforward deterministic action against a marketing system. This requires no AI; L0 is sufficient.
data.errorHandling: Retry transient marketing-platform errors with exponential backoff; if the campaign is unavailable, tag the lead for deferred enrollment and alert marketing ops.

data.label: Flag for Manual Review
data.description: Mark mid-range leads for review by the sales team.
data.rationale: Flagging a record for human review is a deterministic status update or queue placement. It is a basic workflow action and does not require AI.
data.errorHandling: If the review queue update fails, retry transiently and then fall back to creating a manual task plus notification; preserve the lead state for later reconciliation.

data.label: Complete Lead Handling
data.description: Finish processing the lead after it is routed, nurtured, or flagged.
data.rationale: This is a terminal workflow state with no decision-making or intelligence involved. It is purely deterministic control flow at L0.
data.errorHandling: Persist final outcome and any fallback status; if a downstream action partially failed, attach the failure reason to the audit trail and mark the workflow for reconciliation.

message: The workflow now includes deterministic validation and routing tools for L0 steps, an ML scoring binding for L1, and LLM generation bindings for the personalized summary step at L3. Conditions have been refined for all branches, with explicit error paths, retry loops for transient integration failures, and safe fallbacks to manual review or deferred processing when upstream systems are unavailable.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a new lead comes in through the website form, validate the email format and check for duplicates in the CRM. Score the lead based on company size, industry, and engagement history. If the score is above 80, route to a sales rep with a personalized summary. If below 40, add to the nurture campaign. For scores in between, flag for manual review by the sales team.
